blockers.title: Live Google OAuth signin/callback URLs on apex host, not canonical www host
evidence: curl -s https://www.galaxysportsedge.com/api/auth/providers (this session) -> signinUrl and callbackUrl both read https://galaxysportsedge.com/... (apex, no www) despite the request itself targeting www
apps/web/lib/auth.ts:25 sets trustHost: true, which does not explain host-header-independent apex URLs -- points to an explicit NEXTAUTH_URL/AUTH_URL environment override
CLAUDE.md's own documented environment-variable table: 'NEXTAUTH_URL ... Must be the exact live canonical host WITH www ... (identical to NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL)'
blockers.impact: If Google Cloud Console's registered redirect URI is www-only (per CLAUDE.md's own OPERATOR instructions), real users attempting Google sign-in receive an OAuth error instead of signing in. If apex is also registered, sign-in may nominally work but violates the single-canonical-host doctrine with unassessed cookie/session risk.
blockers.blastRadius: Every user attempting Google OAuth sign-in on the live site, right now, until fixed.
blockers.canonicalOwner: Founder (Vercel production environment variables + Google Cloud Console OAuth client)
blockers.smallestSafeFix: Set NEXTAUTH_URL/AUTH_URL to https://www.galaxysportsedge.com on Vercel (production scope); confirm Google Cloud Console's Authorized redirect URIs includes https://www.galaxysportsedge.com/api/auth/callback/google.
blockers.verification: Re-fetch /api/auth/providers after the change; confirm both URLs read the www host. Ideally follow with one real (or test-account) Google sign-in round-trip.
blockers.rollback: Revert the environment variable to its prior value.
blockers.note: Not caught by the prior 17:18 UTC baseline (docs/genesis/LIVE_PRODUCTION_BASELINE_2026-07-18.md) -- new finding this session.

blockers.title: Refund promise contradiction: pricing promises unconditional 3-day guarantee, Terms says discretionary-only

blockers.impact: A paying customer who reads the pricing page and requests a refund within 3 days has a reasonable expectation of an unconditional refund; the Terms page, if actually enforced as written, would let support decline it. Real legal/commercial/trust exposure on the revenue path.
blockers.blastRadius: Every paid-tier signup; realized only if/when a refund is requested and support follows the Terms language over the pricing promise.
blockers.canonicalOwner: Founder (legal/commercial policy decision: which promise is the real one)

blockers.verification: After the fix lands and deploys: automated cross-surface test asserting pricing/checkout/FAQ/tier-panel/Terms/support copy all cite the identical refund policy.
blockers.reEntryCondition: Founder decides the canonical refund policy (unconditional 3-day, or discretionary, or some third option).
